SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DRAWING MAKING TECHNIQUES

This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Drawing MAKING TECHNIQUES helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: DRAWING MAKING TECHNIQUES
Study Drawing MAKING TECHNIQUES like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Appreciate own and others technique drawn work . • Display their work and comment on own and others work

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate own and others technique drawn work . • Display their work and comment on own and others work. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate own and others technique drawn work . • Display their work and comment on own and others work.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Drawing MAKING TECHNIQUES” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate own and others technique drawn work . • Display their work and comment on own and others work. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Drawing MAKING TECHNIQUES is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Drawing MAKING TECHNIQUES” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: appreciate own and others technique drawn work . • Display their work and comment on own and others work)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Drawing MAKING TECHNIQUES to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: appreciate own and others technique drawn work . • Display their work and comment on own and others work.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Drawing MAKING TECHNIQUES from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Drawing MAKING TECHNIQUES: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Drawing MAKING TECHNIQUES?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

3. What material do you , simple pictures using use for drawing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Drawing MAKING TECHNIQUES means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: appreciate own and others technique drawn work . • Display their work and comment on own and others work.
